text.p: Goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert, who has made a habit of scoring goals as well as stopping them, struck again on Wednesday, scoring from a free kick for his Argentine club side Velez Sarsfield.

The charismatic Paraguayan international opened the scoring to set his team on the way to a 3-0 win at home to Olimpia, a Paraguayan team, in a South American Supercup quarter-final first leg tie in Buenos Aires.
In what has almost become a routine event, Chilavert ran the entire length of the pitch as soon as Velez were awarded a free kick on the edge of the Olimpia penalty area in the 19th minute.
He then blasted a left foot shot which evaded the defensive wall and went under the body of rival goalkeeper Jorge Battaglia.
Chilavert scored four goals -- two from penalties and two from free kicks -- as Velez Sarsfield won the Argentine championship held in the first half of this year.
He also scored from a free kick as his country held Argentina to a 1-1 draw in a World Cup qualifier in Buenos Aires in September and has since converted another penalty for his club.
However, last week he was upstaged when Venezuela goalkeeper Rafael Dudamel scored from a free kick in a World Cup qualifier against Argentina.
Chilavert, a national hero in his own country, was given a standing ovation, both by the Argentine Velez fans and the Paraguayans who had come to support Olimpia.
Patricio Camps and Christian Bassedas scored further goals for Velez as the Paraguayan side, who eliminated Sao Paulo of Brazil in the first round, were swamped.

In the night's other quarter-final, first leg tie, Brazil's Santos, who have had a miserable run in their own championship, beat Colombians Atletico Nacional with first-half goals by strikers Jean and Jamelli.
The game marked the return of goalkeeper Edinho, the son of Pele, to the Santos team. Edinho had been left out of previous Supercup games in favour of his understudy Sergio.
